probe: PROBE 2 - does KeeperHub broadcast a transaction it predicts will revert
hypothesis: simulate:false should broadcast even a guaranteed-revert call, giving the demo a real tx hash for negative-control evidence

trial_A_contract_call.result: NOT broadcast. No executionId, no transactionHash, nothing on-chain.

trial_B_check_and_execute.result: Condition passed (value() >= 0 is trivially true), but the ACTION leg was still pre-simulated and rejected before broadcast. No executionId, no transactionHash.

trial_C_node_write_contract.note: actionType catalog reverse-engineered by brute-checking plausible <plugin>/<kebab-case-node> strings (docs did not enumerate them). Confirmed valid: code/run-code, web3/approve-token, web3/transfer-token, web3/read-contract, web3/write-contract. This is the workflow-node action-config schema (abiFunction, not functionName - matches plan.md's documented issue #1927 gotcha), distinct from the Direct Execution REST schema.

response.error: Insufficient BASE balance. Have: 0.0, Need: 0.000000231. Fund 0x5515844b92dd96c3298fd7d62fb87cee279f18d3 with at least 0.000000231 BASE on this chain and retry.

attempt_1_unfunded.finding: This path is NOT gas-sponsored (unlike Direct Execution contract-call/check-and-execute) - it requires the agent EOA to hold native gas itself. Also notable: it got PAST revert-prediction to a funding check, unlike trial A/B which rejected boom() immediately.

fundingTx.action: sent 0.00005 ETH from the deployer wallet to the agent wallet (0x5515844b92dd96c3298fd7d62fb87cee279f18d3) on Base Sepolia to unblock the test

onChainCheck.meaning: nonce did not advance - no transaction was broadcast

attempt_2_funded.finding: Once funded, still pre-simulated and rejected before broadcast, identical failure mode to trial A/B. transactionHash is explicitly null in the status response.

verdict: KILL CONDITION HIT, and now broadly confirmed. Three independent execution paths tested - Direct Execution contract-call, check-and-execute's action leg, and the node/web3-write-contract action (the same schema real workflow action nodes use) - all three refuse to broadcast a call they predict will revert. simulate:false and having real gas in the signer wallet both make no difference. This looks like platform-wide behavior, not a quirk of one endpoint.
impact: Breaks the literal mechanism behind PRD F2 ('>=2 deliberately-broadcast REJECTION transactions, verified') and the write-up's central evidentiary claim ('agent tries, chain refuses, transaction has a hash'), AS EXECUTED THROUGH KEEPERHUB SPECIFICALLY (Direct Execution or a workflow action node with this same actionType). The underlying claim ('the contract itself refuses on a healthy position') is still real and independently provable by any caller (see Foundry test suite: every Refused_* error has a passing test) - what breaks is specifically getting KeeperHub to be the one broadcasting a doomed call and producing the tx hash.
remainingUntested: A real event-triggered workflow (W1 guard, Event trigger -> AnswerUpdated) has not been built and fired live. It's plausible - though now less likely given trial C uses the same underlying action schema - that a genuine workflow run behaves differently from calling the node action directly via REST. This is the one avenue left before concluding the platform categorically cannot produce this evidence.
